title: UBS Sees Mis-Pricing in Equity Markets
description: Feb.17 -- Bhanu Baweja, chief strategist at UBS, discusses the outlook for equities amid the coronavirus outbreak and expectations of central bank liquidity boost to markets. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance."

asr.full_text: You say, look, I don't know if you used the word cost, but it felt like you were saying we could be on the cusp of a recession. If you look at the markets, are they behaving the way they should be? We are at 2.9% global growth is where we are, recession's somewhere close to 2.6% so we have a little bit of buffer. The hope is, and our forecast, base case forecasts, that in Q2 we'll see a decent rebound in global growth so we're not forecasting a recession. But if this wants to persist into Q2, WILL SEE A DECENT REBOUND IN GLOBAL GROWTH. SO WE AREN'T FORECASTING A RECESSION. BUT IF THIS WERE TO PURSURE IN THE Q2, THEN OF COURSE WE WOULD GO INTO A RECESSION. ACROSS THE ASSET CLASSES, THE BOND MARKET'S ARE TELLING YOU THAT WE ARE HEADED THERE. THE EQUITY MARKETS ARE NOT. THE BASE METAL ARENA HAS BEEN THE ONE THAT HAS BEEN HIT THE MOST. THAT'S TO SAY THAT COPPER IS STRUGGLING TO REBOUND. COMMODITIES IN GENERAL, OIL IS STRUGGLING TO REBOUND. BOND PRICES ARE STILL VERY, VERY BAD. EQUITIES ARE TELLING YOU THIS IS A SHOCK. that studies from copper is struggling to rebound our commodities in general oil is struggling to rebound bond bond prices are are still very very big risk-taking the telling you this is a shot men and through it's a very sort of dysmone messages across different an ass at cases it is because the you know equities must more difficult price was actually you know if China collapses or a significant slow sound that it impacts that the you know the demand for oil strength away was it because it they're looking at Fed. I think they are looking at liquidity more than anything else because if you look within equities than some of the growth stocks which are mostly to the liquidity have done much better than the value stocks where the value stocks are about our energy prices rising our steel prices rising our auto sales going up and those stocks have been coming down, whereas the growth stocks, tech and liquidity driven growth stocks have been quite bad. So I think the market is looking for much more liquidity from global central banks. You've seen Fed pricing changed quite a lot, and I think that's why equities have been... OK, but are they right in doing it? Or is the market mispricing? I do think that the market is mispricing. If this was to continue into Q2, equities would prove to be very wrong. OK, let me bring prove to be very wrong. Okay, let me bring you to the chart which we've called now the Banova Wager Chart. So this is thank you to Hilary Clark that brought this to my attention this morning. And it's basically the correlation between gold and the dollar, and that it's a negative correlation at an eight year low. What does that tell us? So, the fact that the correlation is not as negative as it used to be tells you that gold and dollar are moving roughly in the same direction, which doesn't typically MAT TELL US? BORIS HENDERSON THE FACT THAT THE CORRELATION IS NOT AS NEGATIVE AS USE TO BE TELLS YOU THAT GOLD AND DALLAR ARE MOVING ROUGHLY IN THE SAME DIRECTION WHICH DOESN'T TIPLY HAPPEN RIGHT SO TYPICALLY IF THIS IS A STRONG DOLLAR ENVIRONMENT YOU WOULD SEE GOLD SELLING OFF THE FACT THAT GOLD IS RALLYING IN THIS DOLLAR ENVIRONMENT TELLS YOU THAT THIS IS NOT A STRONG DOLLAR ENVIRONMENT THAT WE SHOULD BE ACTUALLY THINKING OF THIS AS A SLIGHTLY WEEK RIMINBI SLIGHTLY WEEK EURO ENVIRONMENT WHICH ARE GRINDING WEAKER BECAUSE THE WORLD IS WORRIED ABOUT GROWTH IN THE REST OF THE WORLD RIGHT SO THIS that we should be actually thinking of this as a slightly weak renminbi slightly weak euro environment which I'm grinding weaker because the world is worried about growth in the rest of the world right so this is not dollar strength this is weakness in other currencies the subject is not the dollar. If therefore growth improves in the rest of the world you will see therefore the dollar weakened. But this changes everything I do think so I mean I think this look if growth in the rest of the world because the corona virus but because also are the reasons that we discussed earlier which is that you're not getting support fiscal or monetary from the rest of the world is that it's correct the over the long term that must impact the dollar side the dollar is going to react the dollar is not the exogenous variable it's not where the story begins is going to react and do weakness in the rest of the world and therefore it's going to be stronger over the medium term. But it's so what does that mean for Fed policy? I think the Fed will therefore have to be a little more dovish. And the market is pricing it. So the market is already saying that it's very interesting, in fact, that after the coronavirus, the RBA, which is much closer to China, the pricing for the RBA didn't change as much as it did for the Fed. So the Fed is now pricing in close to two cuts, which I think is quite a lot for the rest of this year in terms of what's being priced in already. We wouldn't be receiving the front end of of the U.S. at this minute. We think Canada, Switzerland, Australia give us better opportunities to receive the front end.
